skills.pageTitle: Data Readout — AI Agent Skill for Claude Code and Codex
skills.blurb: Turns the numbers you already own into a readout you can act on: it opens the real file first, then gives findings with the business implication of each, chart specs and the caveats that matter.

pageSource.description: Raw numbers turned into a decision: dataset interpretation, statistics with the business implication of each finding, chart specifications, pattern and anomaly detection, forecasts built on stated assumptions, segmentation, A/B test significance, dashboard metric selection and report templates, output as an executive summary, findings ranked by impact and the specific actions they support. Use whenever someone brings data, a spreadsheet, a CSV, an analytics export, an A/B result or an unexpected number and asks what it means, what to chart, whether the test won or which metrics to track, even if they never say analysis. Not for writing the pandas or R code that crunches the file (use production-code), for market research outside the user's own data (use research-brief) or for the strategic roadmap that follows (use strategy-memo).

skills.name: crash-test
skills.title: Crash Test
skills.blurb: Crash-tests a decision before you build it. Four fixed roles draft the same task in separate contexts and attack each other's drafts anonymously; the chair merges what survived on evidence, not votes, keeps a dissent log for what it could not settle, and grounds the winner's claims about your files against the source before adopting them.
skills.stats: 4 roles · ~9 calls · 1 opt-in Operator seat · 2 modes · 0 API keys

skills.name: do-better
skills.title: Do Better
skills.blurb: When an answer is bad, don't ask twice: N sub-agents (100 by default, 16 with --quick) get the exact same task with different strategy cards, then attack, defend and judge each other in a single-elimination bracket until one solution survives.
skills.stats: 2,160 strategy cards · 7 rounds at full size · ~1,700 lines · 0 API keys

skills.name: strategy-memo
skills.title: Strategy Memo
skills.pageTitle: Strategy Memo — AI Agent Skill for Claude Code and Codex
skills.blurb: Turns a business question into a decision document: situation analysis, a recommendation written as ranked options, the risks, and a roadmap someone can execute.

pageSource.description: Business strategy written as a decision document: competitive analysis, market and customer research, business model canvas, growth and pricing strategy, go-to-market plan, SWOT ranked by actionability, ninety-day, one-year and three-year roadmaps, board presentations and pivot assessments, structured as situation analysis, recommendation and execution roadmap. Use whenever someone faces a business decision: should I enter this market, who are my competitors, how should I price this, a go-to-market plan, build me a roadmap, is this worth more investment or a pivot, I need a board deck, even if they never say strategy. Not for pressure-testing a decision you already made (use crash-test), the copy or pages that execute it (use sales-copy, platform-content), or the numbers behind it (use data-readout).

skills.name: solo-income-blueprint
skills.title: Solo Income Blueprint
skills.pageTitle: Solo Income Blueprint — AI Agent Skill for Claude Code and Codex
skills.blurb: Turns “I want to make money online” into one plan: a business model that fits your skills, time and budget, one offer, a demand check, a minimal tool stack and a seven-day launch.

pageSource.description: Design a realistic one-person online income plan from the user's skills, time and budget: one recommended business model, one offer, a demand check, a content and sales path, automations, a minimal tool stack, and a 7-day launch plan. Use when someone asks how to make money online or with AI tools, what to sell, which business model fits them, how to turn a skill they already have into income, how to get a first paying customer, or wants a step-by-step plan for a side business or one-person business. Not for job hunting (application-pilot, applicant-kit), SEO for an existing site (seo-audit), or privacy and legal pages (paper-trail).

skills.name: topic-primer
skills.title: Topic Primer
skills.blurb: A world-class teacher for any topic, from zero background toward expert depth. Eight modes: foundations, full curriculum, concept-by-concept lessons, adaptive tutoring, expert mental models, mistake prevention, strict exams, and ELI5. One question at a time, then it waits.

skills.name: study-system
skills.title: Study System
skills.pageTitle: Study System — AI Agent Skill for Claude Code and Codex
skills.blurb: Builds the system around a skill you are acquiring: the minimum components, a beginner-to-practitioner roadmap, deliberate practice, spaced repetition and an honest mastery check.

pageSource.description: A personal system for acquiring a skill: decomposition into the minimum viable components, a beginner-to-practitioner roadmap, the mental models that unlock a subject, Feynman-level explanations, deliberate-practice routines, knowledge-gap audits that surface wrong assumptions, spaced-repetition schedules, application exercises and honest mastery assessments of where the learner actually is. Use whenever someone has a skill already in progress and needs the structure around it, asks how to practise, how long a skill takes, what they are missing, for a study plan or revision schedule, or says they keep forgetting what they read, even if they never say curriculum. Not for being taught the topic itself concept by concept (use topic-primer), for career positioning and moves (use career-track) or for course content written for a class of students (use course-builder).

skills.name: course-builder
skills.title: Course Builder
skills.pageTitle: Course Builder — AI Agent Skill for Claude Code and Codex
skills.blurb: A course for a class or cohort: measurable outcomes, modules in prerequisite order, an assessment for every outcome and a time budget that fits, checked by a script before the first session.

pageSource.description: Designs a course for a group of learners (a class, cohort, workshop series, bootcamp or internal training): measurable outcomes, a module sequence with prerequisites, activities and assessments aligned to each outcome, a time budget that fits the hours available, and a rubric, then checks the plan with a script so no outcome goes untaught or unassessed. Use when someone is teaching others and asks for a curriculum, syllabus, course outline, module plan, cohort or workshop structure, or wants an existing course checked for gaps and overload, even if they never say "curriculum". Not for one person's own learning plan (use study-system), for being taught the topic (use topic-primer), or for marketing the course (use sales-copy).
